A credit score.

Decades of behavior,
one number.

Your home. Your car. Your interest rate.
That number can shape them all.

Records became power.

But power for the banks.

The best game critics
were never hired.

They're in Discord servers,
comment sections,
group chats.

Talent is everywhere.

Infrastructure wasn't.

Most players have opinions
about every game they play.

Fewer than 1 in 10
ever write them down.

The barrier isn't laziness.

It's "why bother?"

On Stack Overflow,
developers have answered
strangers' questions for free
for over 15 years.

Why?

Because reputation follows them
into job interviews.

GitHub's contribution graph.

Just a grid of green squares.

Yet developers reorganize
their lives to keep the streak.

Visible records
change behavior.
